question: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents for evaluation of easy bruising. He has met all developmental milestones. Vital signs are within normal limits. He is at the 50th percentile for height and weight. Physical examination shows velvety, fragile skin that can be stretched further than normal and multiple ecchymoses. Joint range of motion is increased. A defect in which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Easy bruising and fragile skin" -> "suggestive of connective tissue disorder" -> "increased joint range of motion" -> "possible Ehlers-Danlos syndrome" -> "defect in collagen synthesis" -> "α-collagen triple helix formation" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Velvety, fragile skin" -> "indicates abnormal collagen structure" -> "increased elasticity and fragility" -> "associated with connective tissue disorders" -> "Ehlers-Danlos syndrome suspected" -> "defect in collagen formation" -> "α-collagen triple helix formation" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Multiple ecchymoses" -> "suggests bleeding disorder" -> "fragile blood vessels" -> "connective tissue involvement" -> "increased joint flexibility" -> "indicates Ehlers-Danlos syndrome" -> "defect in collagen structure" -> "α-collagen triple helix formation" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Fragile skin and easy bruising" -> "indicates possible connective tissue disorder" -> "increased joint mobility" -> "characteristic of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome" -> "defect in collagen synthesis" -> "α-collagen triple helix formation" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Child with easy bruising" -> "fragile skin noted on examination" -> "increased joint range of motion" -> "suggests connective tissue disorder" -> "Ehlers-Danlos syndrome considered" -> "defect in collagen structure" -> "α-collagen triple helix formation" -> 80%
analysis: The symptoms described, including easy bruising, velvety and fragile skin, increased joint range of motion, and multiple ecchymoses, are characteristic of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS), particularly the hypermobile type. This condition is often associated with defects in collagen synthesis or structure. The most relevant defect in this context is related to the formation of collagen, specifically the triple helix formation of collagen molecules, which is crucial for the structural integrity of connective tissues. Therefore, the defect in α-collagen triple helix formation is the most likely cause of this patient's condition.
